html:
An uprising against Chinese rule in the Red River delta of northern Vietnam, led from 40 to 43 CE by two sisters, Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị. They are still the best loved heroines of Vietnamese history.

The delta had been part of the Han Empire since the conquest of Nanyue in 111 BCE. The sisters were daughters of a Lạc lord from Mê Linh. When the Han governor pressed the local nobles harder, Trưng Trắc raised a revolt, which later Vietnamese tradition ties to the killing of her husband. Many towns joined them, and Trưng Trắc ruled as queen for about two years.

In 42 the Han sent the general Ma Yuan with a large army. He defeated the rebels in 43. Chinese sources say the sisters were captured and beheaded; Vietnamese tradition says they drowned themselves. Ma Yuan then tightened Han control over the old Lạc nobility. Two centuries later Lady Triệu led another revolt, and both are honoured as founders of a long tradition of resistance that runs to the kingdom of Đại Việt and modern Vietnam.
sum: An uprising against Chinese rule in the Red River delta of northern Vietnam, led from 40 to 43 CE by two sisters, Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị. They are still the best loved heroines of Vietnamese history.
